healthEffects: Silicosis, chronic bronchitis, lung cancer (Group 1 carcinogen), and increased susceptibility to tuberculosis from chronic inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust.
recommendedControls: Substitute lower-silica-content materials where feasible; use wet cutting/wet sawing methods; apply local exhaust ventilation at the point of generation; enclose dust-generating processes.
ppeRecommendations: NIOSH-approved respiratory protection selected per the assigned protection factor for the measured or anticipated exposure concentration; safety glasses; disposable coveralls when dust loading is heavy.
atmosphericMonitoring: Personal breathing-zone air sampling for respirable dust per NIOSH Method 7500 (X-ray diffraction) or equivalent; periodic area monitoring near cutting/grinding operations.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Any N95 or better disposable filtering facepiece respirator
respiratorMatrix.notes: Fit testing required; disposable respirators not adequate above 10x REL.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Half-mask elastomeric respirator with P100 filters, or PAPR with HE filter
respiratorMatrix.notes: Consider PAPR for extended-duration tasks to reduce heat/breathing resistance burden.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Full-facepiece PAPR with HE filter, or SCBA
respiratorMatrix.notes: Confirm concentration is not IDLH before selecting air-purifying respirator.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: Resistance to particulate penetration; low-linting fabric
ppeGuidance.limitations: Not effective against liquid chemical splash; single-use, discard after heavy dust loading.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: ANSI Z87.1 impact and dust rating
ppeGuidance.limitations: Goggles preferred over glasses in high-dust environments to prevent gap infiltration.

healthEffects: Central nervous system depression (headache, dizziness, fatigue, narcosis), eye and mucous membrane irritation, and potential developmental effects from chronic solvent vapor inhalation exposure.
recommendedControls: Substitute with lower-toxicity solvents where feasible; use closed-transfer systems; provide local exhaust ventilation at open containers and mixing/coating operations; store in flammable-rated cabinets.
ppeRecommendations: Chemical splash goggles; nitrile or other solvent-resistant gloves selected per breakthrough-time data; respiratory protection when engineering controls cannot keep vapor concentrations below the REL.
atmosphericMonitoring: Personal breathing-zone sampling per NIOSH Method 1501 (charcoal tube, GC); direct-reading photoionization detector for real-time screening near open transfer points.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Half-mask air-purifying respirator with organic vapor cartridges
respiratorMatrix.notes: Cartridge change-out schedule must account for toluene's poor odor-threshold warning properties.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Full-facepiece air-purifying respirator with organic vapor cartridges, or PAPR with organic vapor cartridges
respiratorMatrix.notes: Full facepiece needed for eye irritation protection at this range.

respiratorMatrix.concentrationRange: Above IDLH (500 ppm) or unknown concentration
respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Supplied-air respirator in pressure-demand mode, or SCBA
respiratorMatrix.notes: Toluene IDLH is 500 ppm; do not rely on air-purifying respirators above this level.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: Breakthrough time greater than task duration per manufacturer permeation data
ppeGuidance.limitations: Natural rubber and PVC gloves offer poor toluene resistance; replace gloves per breakthrough schedule, not visible degradation alone.
Does not protect against vapor inhalation; must be paired with respiratory protection or ventilation controls.

healthEffects: Musculoskeletal disorders including tendinitis, carpal tunnel syndrome, and low-back injury associated with repetitive motion, sustained awkward postures, and manual lifting beyond recommended limits.
recommendedControls: Apply the NIOSH Lifting Equation to evaluate and redesign manual lifting tasks; provide mechanical lift-assist devices; rotate workers among tasks to limit repetitive-motion exposure duration; adjust workstation height to neutral posture.
ppeRecommendations: Anti-fatigue matting for prolonged standing tasks; back-support use is not a NIOSH-recommended substitute for engineering controls.
ergonomicFactors: Repetition rate, force/load magnitude, awkward posture duration, vibration exposure, and insufficient recovery time between exertions, evaluated per the NIOSH Revised Lifting Equation and applicable checklist tools.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: Reduces static loading during prolonged standing tasks
ppeGuidance.limitations: Administrative/comfort measure only; does not substitute for task redesign or lift-assist engineering controls.

healthEffects: Respiratory irritation, olfactory fatigue masking the hazard at higher concentrations, rapid unconsciousness, and death from respiratory paralysis at high airborne concentrations; classified as an immediately dangerous to life or health (IDLH) atmospheric hazard.
recommendedControls: Test and continuously monitor the atmosphere before and during confined-space entry; provide continuous mechanical ventilation of the space; implement a permit-required confined space program with attendant and rescue provisions.
ppeRecommendations: Supplied-air respiratory protection or SCBA for any entry where hydrogen sulfide concentration is unknown or may exceed the ceiling limit; flame-resistant clothing where co-located ignition hazards exist.
atmosphericMonitoring: Continuous direct-reading electrochemical or infrared gas detection for hydrogen sulfide, oxygen, and combustible gas prior to and throughout confined-space entry, per NIOSH confined-space entry guidance.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Full-facepiece SCBA or supplied-air respirator with escape SCBA
respiratorMatrix.notes: Hydrogen sulfide's IDLH is 100 ppm; air-purifying respirators are not recommended for confined-space entry given rapid onset of unconsciousness.
Entry above IDLH requires standby rescue team and retrieval system per confined-space entry procedures.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: Audible/visual alarm at or below the 10 ppm ceiling
ppeGuidance.limitations: Point-of-detection device only; does not replace pre-entry atmospheric testing of the space.

healthEffects: Transmission of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, and other bloodborne pathogens through exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials via needlestick, sharps injury, or mucous membrane/non-intact skin contact.
recommendedControls: Use engineering controls such as sharps-injury-prevention devices and sharps disposal containers; implement standard/universal precautions; provide hepatitis B vaccination to workers with occupational exposure.
ppeRecommendations: Disposable gloves for all tasks with potential blood/OPIM contact; fluid-resistant gown and face shield or mask/goggles combination where splash or spray is reasonably anticipated.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: Meets ASTM D6319 (nitrile) or equivalent barrier standard for bloodborne pathogen protection
ppeGuidance.limitations: Single-use; must be changed between patients/tasks and upon visible damage or contamination.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: AAMI barrier level appropriate to anticipated splash/spray exposure
ppeGuidance.limitations: Selection depends on anticipated fluid volume and pressure; standard gowns are not rated for high-splash procedures.

healthEffects: Neurological effects, anemia, kidney damage, and reproductive/developmental toxicity from chronic inhalation or ingestion exposure to inorganic lead dust or fume; bioaccumulates with a long biological half-life.
recommendedControls: Use wet methods or HEPA-filtered vacuum for cleanup instead of dry sweeping or compressed air; provide local exhaust ventilation at lead-generating processes; require handwashing and prohibit eating/smoking in lead work areas; implement a medical surveillance and blood-lead monitoring program.
ppeRecommendations: NIOSH-approved respiratory protection selected per exposure assessment; disposable or laundered protective clothing; separate storage of street clothes from work clothes to prevent take-home contamination.
atmosphericMonitoring: Personal breathing-zone air sampling for lead per NIOSH Method 7300 (ICP) or 7082 (AAS); periodic surface wipe sampling in work and break areas.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Half-mask air-purifying respirator with P100 filters
respiratorMatrix.notes: Fit testing and medical clearance required before respirator assignment.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Full-facepiece air-purifying respirator with P100 filters, or PAPR with HE filter
respiratorMatrix.notes: Fume-generating operations (e.g., torch cutting of leaded coatings) favor PAPR for comfort during extended tasks.

respiratorMatrix.recommendedRespirator: Supplied-air respirator in pressure-demand mode, or SCBA
respiratorMatrix.notes: Abrasive blasting of leaded coatings in enclosures typically requires supplied-air respiratory protection.

ppeGuidance.performanceCriteria: Particulate-resistant fabric; laundered on-site or by a service that handles contaminated garments
ppeGuidance.limitations: Workers must not launder lead-contaminated clothing at home due to take-home contamination risk.
